title: The 10 Best OBD2 Scanners
subtitle: Code readers, Bluetooth adapters and ABS/SRS scan tools for 1996-and-newer vehicles, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An OBD2 scanner plugs into the port under your dash and tells you why the check engine light is on, before you pay a shop to tell you. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (live data, ABS and airbag codes, Bluetooth to a phone app, and bidirectional tests). Basic code readers cover the engine and emissions; full scan tools also read brakes, airbags and the transmission. They run from about $23 for MOTOPOWER's code reader to $350 for Innova's bidirectional 5610.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

buyers_guide.q: Will an OBD2 scanner work on my car?
buyers_guide.a: Every car and light truck sold in the U.S. since 1996 has an OBD2 port, usually under the dashboard near the steering column. Basic engine codes work on all of them; ABS, airbag and other system coverage varies by brand and year.

A code reader reads and clears check engine codes. A scan tool adds live sensor data, and the better ones read ABS, airbag, transmission and TPMS codes. If you've had a brake or airbag light, you need a scan tool.
Handhelds plug in and work with no phone or account. Bluetooth adapters are smaller and use your phone's screen and an app, which can add repair reports, logging and vehicle-specific features.

buyers_guide.q: Should I clear the check engine light?
buyers_guide.a: Only after fixing the problem. Clearing the code turns off the light, but it also resets the emissions monitors, and the car may fail an inspection until they're ready again.

A bidirectional tool can send commands to the car, such as turning on the fuel pump, cycling ABS valves or retracting an electronic parking brake. It's useful for testing parts, not just reading what's wrong.
